title: SAT 12 · Parity
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Sum With Different Parities
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A student adds the whole numbers \(28\) and \(17\). Which statement correctly describes the sum? Choose A or B and explain why.
questions.explanation: The sum is \(28+17=45\). Since \(45=2\times22+1\), it is one more than an even number and is therefore odd. This also follows from the rule that an even number plus an odd number is odd. Choice B incorrectly calls the odd sum even.
questions.hint: Find the sum, then decide whether it splits into two equal whole-number halves, or use the parity rule for even plus odd.

questions.title: Adding Three Consecutive Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Three consecutive whole numbers begin with \(14\). What is their sum? Choose A or B and show the addition.
questions.explanation: The three consecutive whole numbers are \(14\), \(15\), and \(16\). Their sum is \(14+15+16=45\). Choice A is one less than the actual total.
questions.hint: Write the three consecutive numbers that start at 14 and add them.

questions.title: Counters in Equal Rows
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A display has \(7\) rows with \(9\) counters in each row. Is the total number of counters even or odd? Choose A or B and justify your answer.
questions.explanation: There are \(7\times9=63\) counters. Since \(63=2\times31+1\), it is odd. Equivalently, an odd number of groups each containing an odd number of counters gives an odd total in this case. Choice A has the correct total but labels its parity incorrectly.
questions.hint: Multiply to find the total, then check whether that total is divisible by 2.

questions.title: Players on Eight Teams
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A school has \(8\) teams, and each team has \(5\) players. Which statement describes the total number of players? Choose A or B and explain the calculation.
questions.explanation: The total is \(8\times5=40\). Because \(40=2\times20\), it is divisible by \(2\) and is even. Choice B gives the correct total but the wrong parity.
questions.hint: Find 8 times 5, then think about whether a product with an even factor can be odd.

questions.title: The Middle of Three Consecutive Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Three consecutive integers have a sum of \(72\). What is the middle integer? The table compares two possible sequences. Choose A or B and explain your reasoning.
questions.explanation: For three consecutive integers, the middle integer is the average of the three numbers. Since \(72\div3=24\), the integers are \(23,24,25\), and their sum is \(72\). Thus the middle integer is \(24\). Choice A is the first integer, not the middle one.

visuals.alt: Two candidate sequences are shown: 23, 24, 25 has sum 72; 24, 25, 26 has sum 75.

questions.hint: For three consecutive integers the middle one equals their average; divide the sum by 3 and check against the table.

questions.title: Adding Six to an Odd Integer
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Let \(n\) be any odd integer. Is \(n+6\) odd or even? Choose A or B and justify the parity result.
questions.explanation: The number \(6\) is even. Adding an even number to an odd number does not change the parity, so \(n+6\) is odd. For example, if \(n=5\), then \(n+6=11\), which is odd. Choice B incorrectly treats adding an even number as changing odd to even.
questions.hint: Decide whether 6 is even or odd, then think about how adding that kind of number affects the parity of n.

questions.title: The Product of Consecutive Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Consider the product \(51\times52\). Which statement must be true? Choose A or B and explain how the two factors determine the product's parity.
questions.explanation: The integers \(51\) and \(52\) are consecutive, so one is odd and the other is even. In particular, \(52\) is divisible by \(2\), and therefore \(51\times52\) is also divisible by \(2\). Its value is \(2652\), which is even. Choice A is false because a product with an even factor must be even.
questions.hint: Check whether either factor is even; one even factor is enough to decide the parity of the product.

questions.title: Two Consecutive Even Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Two consecutive positive even integers have a sum of \(46\). The table shows two candidate pairs. Which pair satisfies both conditions? Choose A or B and explain why the difference between consecutive even integers is important.
questions.explanation: Consecutive positive even integers differ by \(2\). The pair \(22,24\) has sum \(46\) and difference \(2\), so it satisfies both conditions. The pair \(20,26\) also sums to \(46\), but its members differ by \(6\), so they are not consecutive even integers. Choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: Both candidate pairs sum to 46, but 22 and 24 differ by 2 while 20 and 26 differ by 6.

questions.hint: Check both conditions in the table: the sum must be 46 and consecutive even integers differ by exactly 2.

questions.title: Parity of a Polynomial with an Even Integer
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Suppose \(n\) is an even integer. Is \(n^2+3n+5\) odd or even? Choose A or B and justify each part of the expression.
questions.explanation: If \(n\) is even, then \(n^2\) is even and \(3n\) is also even. The sum of two even numbers is even, so \(n^2+3n\) is even. Adding \(5\), an odd number, makes the result odd. Choice B incorrectly treats the addition of the final odd term as preserving even parity.
questions.hint: Find the parity of each term separately when n is even, then combine them one at a time.

questions.title: The Middle of Five Consecutive Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Five consecutive integers have a sum of \(135\). What is the middle integer? The table compares candidate sequences. Choose A or B and show how the sum identifies the middle.
questions.explanation: In a sequence of five consecutive integers, the middle integer is the average of all five. The average is \(135\div5=27\), so the sequence is \(25,26,27,28,29\). Its sum is \(135\), confirming the result. Choice A would give the sequence \(24,25,26,27,28\), whose sum is \(130\), not \(135\).

visuals.alt: The sequence 25 through 29 has sum 135 and middle 27; the sequence 24 through 28 has sum 130 and middle 26.

questions.hint: For five consecutive integers the middle one is the average; divide the sum by 5 and compare with the table.

questions.title: The Product of a Number and Its Successor
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For every integer \(n\), the numbers \(n\) and \(n+1\) are consecutive. Which statement about \(n(n+1)\) is always true? The table shows the two possible parity cases. Choose A or B and explain why the result holds for every integer.
questions.explanation: Two consecutive integers cannot both be odd or both be even: one must be even. Therefore at least one of the factors in \(n(n+1)\) is divisible by \(2\), making the product even. The table checks both cases. Choice A is false because the product always includes an even factor.

visuals.alt: If n is even, n+1 is odd and the product is even; if n is odd, n+1 is even and the product is also even.

questions.hint: Look at the table's two cases and notice what one of two consecutive integers must always be.

questions.title: The Middle Pair of Four Consecutive Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Four consecutive integers have a sum of \(202\). What are the two middle integers? Choose A or B and justify how the total determines the sequence.
questions.explanation: Four consecutive integers with sum \(202\) have an average of \(202\div4=50.5\). The two middle consecutive integers must be \(50\) and \(51\), making the full sequence \(49,50,51,52\). Its sum is \(202\), and the middle pair is \(50,51\). Choice B gives the two endpoints, not the middle integers.
questions.hint: Divide the sum by 4 to find the average; for four consecutive integers the average lies halfway between the two middle ones.

questions.title: Can Two Consecutive Odd Numbers Sum to Forty-One?
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A student claims that two consecutive odd whole numbers can have a sum of \(41\). Is the claim possible? Choose A or B and explain using the parity of the sum.
questions.explanation: Every odd number plus another odd number has an even sum. For example, consecutive odd whole numbers such as \(19\) and \(21\) sum to \(40\), not an odd number. Since \(41\) is odd, it cannot be the sum of two odd numbers. Choice B is not valid because \(20\) is even and \(21\) is odd; they are not both odd.
questions.hint: Think about the parity of the sum of two odd numbers, and check whether both numbers in option B are odd.

questions.title: The Endpoints of Five Consecutive Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Five consecutive whole numbers have a sum of \(80\). What are the smallest and largest numbers? The table compares two sequences. Choose A or B and justify your answer.
questions.explanation: The average of five consecutive whole numbers is the middle number. Since \(80\div5=16\), the sequence must be \(14,15,16,17,18\). Its smallest number is \(14\) and its largest is \(18\). Choice A describes the endpoints of a different sequence, \(13,14,15,16,17\), whose sum is \(75\).

visuals.alt: The sequence 13 through 17 sums to 75; the sequence 14 through 18 sums to 80 and has endpoints 14 and 18.

questions.hint: Divide the sum by 5 to find the middle number, then count two steps down and two steps up.

questions.title: A Pair of Consecutive Even Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Two consecutive positive even integers have a sum of \(118\). Which pair is correct? Choose A or B and explain why both the sum and the gap matter.
questions.explanation: The two numbers have average \(118\div2=59\). The even integers immediately below and above \(59\) are \(58\) and \(60\), which sum to \(118\) and differ by \(2\). Choice A also sums to \(118\), but its numbers differ by \(6\), so they are not consecutive even integers.
questions.hint: Find the average of the two numbers, then pick the even integers just below and above it and check their gap.

questions.title: The Middle of Three Consecutive Positive Integers
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Three consecutive positive integers have a product of \(210\). What is the middle integer? Choose A or B and verify the product.
questions.explanation: The consecutive positive integers \(5,6,7\) have product \(5\times6\times7=210\), so the middle integer is \(6\). The neighboring possible triple \(6,7,8\) has product \(336\), not \(210\). As the factors increase together for positive consecutive integers, no other positive triple gives the stated product. Choice B is therefore incorrect.
questions.hint: Estimate the middle integer from the cube root of 210, then test the product of the triple around it.

questions.title: Consecutive Integers with a Fixed Sum of Squares
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Two consecutive positive integers have a sum of squares equal to \(365\). Which pair satisfies the condition? The table compares two candidates. Choose A or B and show the calculation.
questions.explanation: For the pair \(13,14\), the sum of squares is \(13^2+14^2=169+196=365\), so it meets the condition. For the pair \(14,15\), the sum is \(196+225=421\), which is too large. More generally, if the smaller integer is \(x\), then \(x^2+(x+1)^2=365\), so \(2x^2+2x+1=365\) and \(x^2+x=182\). Thus \((x-13)(x+14)=0\); because \(x\) is positive, \(x=13\). Choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: The squares of 13 and 14 sum to 365; the squares of 14 and 15 sum to 421.

questions.hint: Compute the sum of squares for each pair in the table, or set up x^2+(x+1)^2 = 365 for the smaller integer x.

questions.title: Finding a Middle Integer from the Endpoint Product
questions.learningObjective: Apply parity and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Three consecutive positive integers have the property that the product of the smallest and largest is \(80\). What is the middle integer? Choose A or B and explain how the two endpoints determine the middle number.
questions.explanation: The positive integers \(8,9,10\) are consecutive, and the product of their endpoints is \(8\times10=80\). Thus the middle integer is \(9\). To verify uniqueness, let the middle integer be \(n\); then the endpoints are \(n-1\) and \(n+1\), so \((n-1)(n+1)=80\), giving \(n^2-1=80\) and \(n^2=81\). Since \(n\) is positive, \(n=9\). Choice A is the smallest integer in the triple, not the middle one.
questions.hint: Call the middle integer n; the endpoints are n-1 and n+1, so their product is a difference of squares.
